gloss: someone like a big brother, senior figure

definitions.gloss: someone in a big-brother role, senior mentor figure
definitions.explanation: A person who acts as a protective older-brother figure in a group or relationship, without necessarily being a blood relative. Implies a combination of seniority, guidance, and camaraderie. Often used in informal or masculine social contexts.

examples.japanese: ⟦{彼|かれ}→彼：01292_kare⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦チーム→チーム：03858_chiimu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{兄貴分|あにきぶん}だ。
examples.english: He's the big-brother figure of the team.

examples.japanese: {兄貴分|あにきぶん}⟦として→として：06802_toshite⟧⟦{後輩|こうはい}→後輩：02501_kouhai⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{面倒|めんどう}を{見|み}ている→面倒を見る：18263_mendouwomiru⟧。
examples.english: As a senior mentor, he looks after the younger members.

examples.japanese: ⟦{入社|にゅうしゃ}した→入社する：25409_nyuushasuru⟧⟦ばかり→〜ばかり：02006_bakari⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{頃|ころ}、{兄貴分|あにきぶん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{先輩|せんぱい}→先輩：01451_senpai⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧いろいろ⟦{教|おし}えて→教える：00526_oshieru⟧⟦もらった→もらう：00520_morau⟧。
examples.english: When I first joined the company, a senior colleague who was like a big brother taught me a lot.

notes:
A compound of ⟦{兄貴|あにき}→兄貴：11623_aniki⟧ (big brother, colloquial) + ⟦{分|ぶん}→分：26216_bun⟧ (role, status, part). The ～⟦{分|ぶん}→分：26216_bun⟧ suffix indicates that the person fills that role without literally being one. The word has a warm, informal tone and is typically used among men.

In yakuza or gang contexts, {兄貴分|あにきぶん} refers to a higher-ranking member who mentors and protects a junior member.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {兄貴分|あにきぶん}⟦として→として：06802_toshite⟧: in the role of big brother
- ⟦チーム→チーム：03858_chiimu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{兄貴分|あにきぶん}: the big brother of the team
- {兄貴分|あにきぶん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{存在|そんざい}→存在：03326_sonzai⟧: a big-brother presence

RELATED WORDS:
- {姉御分|あねごぶん}: big-sister figure — the female equivalent
- ⟦{兄貴|あにき}→兄貴：11623_aniki⟧: big brother — informal/colloquial term for an older brother or older male figure
- ⟦{先輩|せんぱい}→先輩：01451_senpai⟧: senior — a broader term for someone senior in an organization or school
